children: New Delhi, Oct. 27 -- The Indian stock market is expected to open lower on Tuesday, October 27, as indicated by GIFT Nifty futures. GIFT Nifty was trading near 22,663, down around 110 points, or 0.48%, from the previous close of Nifty futures, signalling a weak start for domestic benchmark indices.

The benchmark Sensex snapped its four-session losing streak on Monday, rising 483 points, while the Nifty 50 reclaimed the 22,750 level amid value buying and gains in metal, telecom and healthcare stocks. The 30-share BSE Sensex recovered from early losses to close 482.92 points, or 0.66%, higher at 73,606.75. The NSE Nifty 50 gained 153.20 points, or 0.68%, to settle at 22,753.20, ending its four-day losing run.

Several stocks are likely to remain in focus during Tuesday's trading session as companies announce key corporate developments. Updates related to order wins, business performance, expansion plans and other company-specific announcements could influence movements in individual stocks.
Larsen & Toubro, Maruti Suzuki, Paytm, DCM Shriram, Tata Consumer among shares in focus on Tuesday.

Shares of Larsen and Toubro, Maruti Suzuki India, Bajaj Auto, Tata Steel, Cipla, Indus Towers, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, JSW Infrastructure, Steel Authority of India, Waaree Energies will remain in focus as companies are scheduled to release their Q2 results 2026 today.

Fintech firm Paytm posted a 976% year-on-year surge in consolidated net profit to Rs.226 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs.21 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from operations climbed 28% year-on-year to Rs.2,648 crore.

The company reported a 17.6% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs.467 crore for Q2 FY27, up from Rs.397 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose 14% to Rs.5,661 crore, while EBITDA grew 16.5% to Rs.783 crore.

The company's net profit declined 21.2% year-on-year to Rs.3,478 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs.4,415 crore in the year-ago quarter. It also announced a second interim dividend of Rs.3.50 per equity share with a face value of Rs.10 for FY27.
The company posted a 34.09% year-on-year drop in net profit to Rs.105 crore in Q2 FY27, even as revenue increased 21% to Rs.4,151 crore.
The bank reported a 41.5% year-on-year jump in net profit to Rs.2,310 crore for the second quarter, compared with Rs.1,633 crore in the corresponding period last year.
The company reported a net loss of Rs.52.3 crore in Q2 FY27, widening from a loss of Rs.21 crore in the same quarter last year.
The company's net profit rose 33.4% quarter-on-quarter to Rs.100.3 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs.75.2 crore in the preceding quarter.
The company received a Letter of Acceptance (LOA) worth approximately Rs.91.78 crore from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
The company posted a net loss of Rs.205 crore in Q2 FY27, against a net profit of Rs.239 crore in the year-ago quarter, including an exceptional one-time loss of Rs.339 crore.
